extracted.intended_audience: government contracting officers, bond approvers, and legal counsel reviewing/accepting bonds for U.S. government contracts (War Department)
extracted.subtask_description: Reviewing, approving, and determining the sufficiency and acceptability of bonds (bid guaranties, performance bonds, indemnity bonds) given to the United States in connection with government contracts and public-property loans, with attention to formalities, surety capacity, and statutory protections for labor and material-men.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond of indemnity when foreign liens possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a vessel was made in a foreign country and it was possible the laws of the country would give labor and material-men a lien, and the act of Congress of August 13, 1894 would not be applicable, a bond might be required to secure the payment of laborers and material-men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require indemnity bond when foreign construction risks local lien claims that federal statute does not cover; use bond to secure potential claims of labor and material-men.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional refund bond pending administrative decision
rubrics_metrics.description: If payments to a contractor are suspended and an appeal is pending, a bond may be accepted conditioned to refund all payments if the decision is adverse, but the refund should not be conditioned upon determination of a question of fact which might have to be referred to the courts for decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept bonds to secure repayment of suspended payments, but avoid bond conditions that postpone refund until contested fact determinations in court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of bond when contractual test cannot be performed
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a test required by a contract could not be applied because work was completed at the wrong season, payment retained may be released upon contractor filing a bond conditioned to make good any defects that might develop upon proper test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When contractual performance cannot be practically tested, accept a bond securing future correction of defects rather than withholding payment indefinitely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond to indemnify officers for use of patented articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Where officers representing the United States used certain patented articles not owned by the contractor from whom obtained, a bond should be required from the contractor before payment, conditioned to indemnify the officers and agents of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If government agents would otherwise be exposed to suit or liability from use of third-party patented items, require contractor indemnity bond to protect officers and agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of a bidder's guaranty
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of a bidder's guaranty is to furnish sufficient security that the bidder will, if his bid is accepted, enter into contract as prescribed; the direct object is to enable the Government to collect the difference between the bidder's bid and the amount the Government would have to pay someone else if the bidder should not enter into contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare the guaranty to be as formal and legally sufficient as a contractor's bond so it can serve as the basis of a legal claim by suit if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of non-fatal defects in bidders' guaranties
rubrics_metrics.description: Such defects in bidders' guaranty bonds as are not fatal to the validity of the bond are in practice waived by the department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departments may waive minor/formal defects that do not affect substantive validity; evaluate materiality before rejecting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waivable restrictions that do not affect validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Where instructions to bidders provided that a partner will not be accepted as a guarantor or surety for a copartner, this objection may be waived since it would not in any way affect the validity of the guaranty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrictions in bidding instructions that are purely discretionary and not jurisdictional may be waived if acceptance does not impair legal enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curing omissions in guaranty blanks by context
rubrics_metrics.description: Omissions in filling out guaranty blanks (e.g., missing time for entering into contract, missing bidder name) may be cured by surrounding documents such as the accompanying proposal which designate the time or by subsequent appearance of the bidder's name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess collateral documents and the overall proposal to determine if blanks are cured; minor omissions may be treated as non-fatal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seal requirement and effect of omission
rubrics_metrics.description: A guaranty defective by omission of a seal may be unenforceable as a sealed instrument (valid without consideration), and if lacking consideration may not be valid as an unsealed instrument; but governing state law may abolish distinctions making omission immaterial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine applicable law (place of contract/execution) for effect of seal omission; in practice War Department commonly requires bonds to be under seal (printed scroll seal accepted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed/scroll seal acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: A printed scroll or other device is recognized in all States and Territories (except some) as a valid substitute for a seal; the War Department will not require an adhesive seal where a scroll seal is customarily used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept adopted printed/scroll seals unless local law of execution place requires physical adhesive seal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporation principal: full legal name required
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a corporation is principal in a bond given to the United States its full legal corporate name should be expressed; otherwise the bond may be incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify corporate formation documents and include the corporation's full statutory name as obligor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate name and seal to be affixed by authorized officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a corporation is named as principal its corporate name and seal (if it has one) should be affixed by the officer having authority to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm officer authority to sign and affix corporate seal; require appropriate officer signature and seal where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: When execution authority unclear for foreign corporations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the principal on a bond was a foreign corporation and there was no evidence the persons who executed it were authorized, and delay to obtain evidence was impracticable, it is recommended the individual sureties be required to sign a statement that the bond is properly executed by and binding upon the principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain surety statements attesting to proper execution to estop sureties from later contesting lack of principal's execution where regular evidence cannot be secured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of corporate seal does not vitiate if some seal used
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that a corporation has not adopted a corporate seal will not affect the validity of its execution of a bond, provided some form of seal be added to its signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept alternative forms of seal or adopted seals; ensure some evidence of a seal is present or adopted by the corporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unincorporated bodies cannot be principal parties
rubrics_metrics.description: An unincorporated body that has no legal entity cannot become a party to a bond; the practice is to require the bond to be signed by a private person as principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If public property is loaned to an unincorporated body, require an individual principal or an appropriate legal entity to execute the bond; include recitals identifying any trading name usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official capacity execution for non-entity governmental boards
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a governmental body is not a legal entity, the proper procedure is to have the governing board pass a resolution authorizing an officer (e.g., treasurer) in his official capacity to execute the bond, which should then be executed by that officer in his official capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require formal board resolution authorizing execution and officer's official-capacity signature to bind a government body lacking separate legal existence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business conducted under company name: use individual's name as principal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an individual conducts business under a company name, a contract and bond should be in the name of the individual and not the mere company name which has no legal existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If trade name only, require bond in the individual's legal name, with condition reciting contract entered under trade name if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligee name must be a legal entity (example: Philippine Islands)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there was no act creating a corporate existence for 'Government of the Philippine Islands,' there was no legal entity capable of being obligee; such bonds should run to 'The United States of America' for the use of the government of the Philippine Islands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure obligee named on bond is a legal entity capable of receiving obligations; when in doubt, run bond to United States 'for the use of' subordinate governments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of witness does not affect bond validity
rubrics_metrics.description: The absence of a witness to the signature of a principal or surety on a bond does not affect the validity of the bond and may be waived where the signature is known to the department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not insist on witness formality if signature can be verified and department chooses to waive; document verification where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dating of bond: omission not fatal
rubrics_metrics.description: A bond should be dated, but omission of the date will not affect the validity of the instrument since the true date of execution can be otherwise proved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept undated bonds when execution date can be proven; prefer dated instruments to avoid later disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistent dates and remedial steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Inconsistencies between bond date and date of board resolution or contract do not necessarily constitute fatal defects, but if dates show improper authority timing, the bond should be reexecuted or ratified as of a proper date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where dates create a question whether authority existed at time of execution, require reexecution or ratification to avoid reliance on outside evidence in litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recital that bond executed before contract not fatal but avoid contradictions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a bond recites it was executed before the contract, that inconsistency does not affect validity because a bond takes effect from delivery; nevertheless, recitals are identification aids and contradictory recitals may warrant requiring a new bond to prevent evidentiary problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer bonds whose recitals accurately establish identity of contract; obtain new bond if recitals would force reliance on parol evidence in suit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity of signatory guarantors (parent or family)
rubrics_metrics.description: A guaranty signed by the father of the bidder is binding on the father; but the War Department advised that a bond subscribed by daughters of a contractor should not be accepted as sureties even if financial relations are satisfactorily explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess capacity and propriety of proposed sureties; familial relationships do not automatically disqualify but some proposed sureties (e.g., daughters, married women) historically not accepted in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict construction of sureties' obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligations incurred by sureties are strictly construed in their favor, and a bond should not be accepted where suit cannot be successfully brought upon it against the sureties; the contract on the face of the instrument must be clearly valid and binding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure bonds are drafted to be enforceable in court and that sureties are competent and clearly bound; avoid accepting bonds with latent defects that would defeat suit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material alterations release sureties
rubrics_metrics.description: If after execution a material change is made in the name or description of the principal by erasure or interlineation without assent of the sureties, the sureties not consenting will be released; recommend obtaining new bond if such alteration occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not permit material post-execution alterations without written consent of sureties; require new bond or written assent to preserve surety liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond does not cover material modifications without sureties' assent
rubrics_metrics.description: A bond for the faithful performance of a contract will not cover material modifications of the contract, in the form of supplemental agreement or otherwise, unless the sureties formally assent to the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain surety consent prior to making material contract modifications; include clause limiting or defining permissible modifications or requiring express surety assent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond covers modifications authorized by contract terms
rubrics_metrics.description: A bond to secure the performance of a contract is valid to secure the performance of any such modifications thereof as are authorized by the terms of the contract itself, but will not cover unauthorized modifications which substantially make a new contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether contract clauses authorize the change; if change is within authorized scope, sureties remain bound; otherwise secure assent or new bond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of contract time discharge sureties without consent
rubrics_metrics.description: A bond cannot be extended beyond the period originally fixed by its terms so as to continue to bind the sureties unless they consent to such extension; granting material delay without surety assent can discharge sureties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not grant time extensions that materially alter surety exposure without securing surety assent; if bond expressly binds during extensions, consult bond language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractual provision binding surety during extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a bond provided that the surety should be bound 'as well during any period of extension of said contract that may be granted ... as during the original term,' the surety would continue to be bound even though the contract was extended more than once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review bond language: express extension-binding provisions will bind surety to agreed extension periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twofold obligation: performance and labor/material protection
rubrics_metrics.description: A contractor's bond may be considered as two obligations—one to secure due performance of the contract and the other to secure payment to labor and material-men—and a modification of the contract without surety consent may not release the obligation on behalf of labor and material-men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that surety liability to third-party labor/material claims can survive certain contract modifications; assess statutory protections (e.g., Aug. 13, 1894) before acting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission of name in body does not affect validity
rubrics_metrics.description: The omission of the name of the principal or surety from the body of the bond does not affect its validity; signature or seal fixes liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on signatures/seals to fix identity; minor internal recital name errors that are reconcilable by signature are non-fatal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of justification formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit of justification should be taken before an officer having authority to administer oaths; if the officer has an official seal it must be affixed; the affidavit should be dated so that it may appear when the surety was worth the amount specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require proper notarial/official administration and a date on the justification affidavit; however, the justification is not part of the bond and irregularities in who administered the oath may be waived if taken in good faith and bond otherwise valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplying omissions after delivery without surety consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where omissions (missing date, names, seals) were supplied after delivery and before approval but whether with surety knowledge/consent was not known, assume omissions were not supplied with consent and require a new bond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If blanks are filled in post-delivery without proof of surety consent, prefer obtaining a new bond rather than risking later defenses that sureties did not consent to changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to obtain one bondsman's consent releases all
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure to secure the consent of one of the bondsmen to the modification of a contract releases not only that bondsman, but all the bondsmen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain unanimous written consents of bondsmen for modifications that would otherwise discharge liability; do not rely on partial consents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of surety death on joint-and-several obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the obligation of a bond is joint and several (as in official bonds), the estate of the deceased surety is not discharged by death and there is no necessity of a new bond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish joint-and-several from joint-only obligations; consult the bond's language to determine survivors' liability and whether re-bonding is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stockholders and officers as sureties
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph of Army Regulations provides stockholders who are not officers of a corporation may be accepted as sureties; directors or members of a board of trustees are 'officers.' The regulation does not apply where a treasurer is not a stockholder and he may be accepted as surety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply departmental regulations regarding corporate officer/stockholder status when accepting corporate sureties; obtain documentation of roles and shareholdings where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of female sureties in practice
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not the practice of the War Department to accept a married woman as surety, and before an unmarried female surety will be accepted she is required to make oath that she is single in addition to justifying as others; affidavit must show she is worth the sum in her own right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically, exercise caution accepting female sureties per departmental practice; require oaths and clear demonstration of personal assets when acceptance is considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governing law: place of making vs performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The law of the place at which a contract was made governs as to its interpretation, obligation and legal effect, except where the contract is to be performed elsewhere, in which case the law of the place of performance governs; formalities of execution and capacity of parties are governed by the law of the place where the contract was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine applicable governing law (making vs performance) for interpretation and formalities; for official bonds to the United States, treat them as contracts to be performed at Washington and governed by District of Columbia law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental exclusive authority over bond approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of taking and approving bonds under the War Department rests entirely in the War Department; the Treasury has no authority to review the War Department's action or pass upon sufficiency of sureties on bonds given under specified statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect departmental allocation of approval authority; seek War Department determination for sufficiency rather than Treasury review when statutory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice on surrendering bonds after performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Even after due performance of bond conditions, it is contrary to the practice of the department to surrender such bonds; if records show all conditions performed bondsmen are so advised, but the department does not typically return accepted bonds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not surrender accepted bonds except where bond was refused by the United States; be cautious about any communication that might be construed as releasing sureties absent statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on executive release of bonds absent statute
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of a statute no executive officer has authority to cancel or nullify a bond or release a surety thereon; such release cannot be given even if other sureties of undoubted financial responsibility are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on administrative releases of sureties without clear statutory authorization; require formal legal process or statute to discharge bonds.
